requirement: The system shall assign a unique sample identifier to each sample registered in the system and shall prevent reuse of the identifier across active and archived sample.

analysis.gamp_rationale: Unique identifier generation and enforcement of uniqueness across active and archived records is a configurable business rule typically found in a LIMS/sample management platform, making it a configured commercial product function rather than custom-coded logic.
analysis.gxp_rationale: Unique sample identification is fundamental to data integrity and traceability; duplicate or reused IDs could cause misattribution of results to the wrong sample, directly impacting product quality and patient safety.
analysis.severity_fact: If identifiers are duplicated or reused, sample results could be linked to the wrong sample, leading to mix-ups, incorrect release/rejection decisions, loss of traceability, and potential patient harm from misidentified test results.
analysis.probability_fact: ID collision or reuse is a well-recognized risk in high-throughput systems, especially at sequence rollover, during archival/restore operations, or in concurrent multi-user registration; without explicit uniqueness enforcement the likelihood is meaningful but such logic is a standard, mature platform capability.
analysis.detectability_fact: A reused or duplicate identifier may not be obvious to an end user during routine use, as the system would typically appear to function normally; detection usually depends on downstream reconciliation or audit rather than an immediate visible error, unless the system actively blocks the duplicate at registration.
